  <h1 id="challenges-title">Challenges</h1>
  <p>Challenges are the short deliverables of the course. Each challenge extends the module adventure and turns guided practice into a personal production: report, graph, cleaning task, function, video or dashboard.</p>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="challenge-role-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="challenge-role-title">Why challenges?</h2>
  <p>Each challenge targets a concrete skill. The goal is to move from understanding to a visible trace of what you can do, in a context close enough to the adventure to be supportive, but different enough to require autonomy.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-hub-grid">
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Autonomy</h3><p>You take a skill seen in the module and apply it in a slightly different context.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Progression</h3><p>Challenges gradually build the reflexes needed for the project and the exam.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Communication</h3><p>The deliverable must be understandable to someone reading your work without being inside your head.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="challenge-map-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="challenge-map-title">Challenge, adventure or exercises?</h2>
  <p>These three elements speak to each other, but they do not have the same role.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">1</span><h3>Adventure</h3><p>Guided in-class work. It sets the context, characters, data and technical skills for the module.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">2</span><h3>Challenge</h3><p>Evaluated continuation of the adventure. You produce a more autonomous trace from the same pedagogical universe.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">3</span><h3>Exercises</h3><p>Separate consolidation. Exercises are for practice, but they are not a required step in the challenge.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">4</span><h3>Feedback</h3><p>The comments you receive help improve future challenges, the exam and the session project.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="submission-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="submission-title">Before submitting</h2>
  <p>The challenge page explains the work to produce. Brio remains the official source for dates, submission locations and administrative details.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article><h3>Instructions</h3><p>Reread the challenge page and identify the files explicitly requested. A strong analysis does not compensate for a missing deliverable.</p><a href="evaluations.html">View assessments</a></article>
  <article><h3>Files</h3><p>Open the final render and check figures, file paths, column names and the data files that must be submitted.</p><a href="boite_outils.html">Prepare your environment</a></article>
  <article><h3>GitHub repository</h3><p>When the challenge uses GitHub, push your commits and reread the online repository as if you were the person grading it.</p><a href="ressources.html">Find resources</a></article>
  <article><h3>Allowed AI Use</h3><p>In challenges and the project, AI is allowed as support for reasoning, debugging, revision, planning or checking. In the exam, only the tools explicitly authorized on Brio are allowed. In all cases, the final deliverable must remain verifiable, personal and consistent with the instructions. You must understand, test and be able to explain any submitted code, text, source, result or interpretation. When AI influences an important part of an evaluated deliverable, keep a short trace: tool used, purpose of help, affected part and verification done. The official requirements posted on Brio always prevail.</p><a href="ia.html">Read the AI page</a></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Challenge 4</h3><p>Insurance dataset cleaning and documentation of decisions.</p><p>Expected trace: clean file, reproducible log and defensible decisions.</p><a href="module_04/defi.html">View challenge 4</a></article>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="challenge-types-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="challenge-types-title">Types of productions</h2>
  <p>Formats vary across modules, but they always remain connected to course skills.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article><h3>Analysis report</h3><p>Import, summarize, visualize and interpret a dataset.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Article or short note</h3><p>Turn an analysis into a clear message for a defined audience.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Data cleaning</h3><p>Document correction, recoding and preparation choices.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Improved graph</h3><p>Revise a visualization so it better supports interpretation.</p></article>
  <article><h3>R function</h3><p>Automate a repetitive task and make code reusable.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Video or dashboard</h3><p>Communicate an analysis in a more interactive or narrative format.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="challenge-method-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="challenge-method-title">Workflow</h2>
  <p>A successful challenge is rarely a long document. It is clear, focused and cleanly rendered.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>Read the full instructions and identify the expected product.</li>
  <li>Return to the module adventure to recover the context, data and useful skills.</li>
  <li>Build a simple first version that works.</li>
  <li>Render the file, test links or output files, then reread as an external reader.</li>
  <li>Submit the right file or repository according to the instructions confirmed on Brio.</li>
  </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Watch points">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Do not over-expand</h3><p>Answer the instructions before adding secondary analyses.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Name choices</h3><p>Briefly explain why a transformation, graph or filter is used.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Check the trace</h3><p>A missing render, misnamed file or unpushed repository can prevent grading.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Reuse feedback</h3><p>Each challenge prepares the next one: keep useful corrections in your notes.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="feedback-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="feedback-title">After feedback</h2>
  <p>A challenge is not only a one-time submission. Comments received help consolidate your methods and prepare longer productions.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-hub-grid">
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Fix one habit</h3><p>Record a recurring code, rendering, graph or interpretation issue so it does not reappear in the next challenge.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Keep a trace</h3><p>Save code, visualization and communication examples that may be reused in the project.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Return to exercises</h3><p>Use the independent exercises to revisit a specific skill without depending on the challenge story.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>
</div>
